Fix: in the `finally`, `signal.signal(sig, previous)` when `previous` is a Python-level handler (the machinery already exists — `_rehonor` does exactly this on the flush path). If `previous` is `_sighandler_noop` (harbor had its own `add_signal_handler` registration), the captured value can't restore the loop callback — in that case prefer *not installing* over half-restoring (skip when `signal.getsignal(sig)` is neither `SIG_DFL` nor `default_int_handler`).

**2. Overlapping trials clobber each other (the workflow exposes `--n-concurrent`).**
`bench-harbor.yml` takes an `n-concurrent` input (default 1, owner-raised for kimi). With >1, two FaAgent trials in one loop each call `loop.add_signal_handler(SIGTERM, ...)` — last install wins, and whichever trial finishes first strips the handler the live trial just installed. On a process SIGTERM only one trial's audit flushes; the others leave `running` checkpoints. If concurrent installs are to be supported, make the install refcounted (module-level registry keyed by signal) or document `n-concurrent=1` as a hard requirement for the SIGTERM path.

- **Title**: gh-1576 [GOAL] Truthful effective deadline: min(external harness cap, fa knobs) — kill the lying 3600s clock (TB 2.1 external-timeout class)
- **Author**: ai-teammate

- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T21:25:26Z

## PR Description

Closes #1576
### What changed

The external harness cap (tb `--global-agent-timeout-sec`, harbor's per-task `[agent] timeout_sec`) is now resolved by the bench adapters and folded into ONE effective deadline — `min(external cap, adapter knobs)` — exported to fa as `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` and recorded truthfully in every audit.

### Key decisions

- `bench/fa_agent_timeout.py` owns resolution: new `CapResolution` (env scan + strict parsing; malformed caps degrade to unknown with a stderr warning) and `resolve_deadline()` as the single source of the effective cap + wrap-up deadline
- Both workflows export the cap: `bench.yml` sets `FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC` = the same number as `--global-agent-timeout-sec` (parity); `bench-harbor.yml` maps `matrix.external_cap` — the MIN of the shard tasks' declared timeouts, resolved pre-launch by `split_tasks.py`; no declared cap ⇒ no export ⇒ knobs rule alone (byte-identical)
- Deciders clamp their kill deadline to the external cap and name the winner (`external_cap`) in the verdict; audits gain `cap` resolution + `deadline_epoch_ms`, and land even on unsupervised external kills (verdict = the harness failure mode — no more bare `AGENT_STATUS_UNSET`)
- Kill-survival hardening: incremental per-sample audit checkpoints survive a SIGKILL; cancellations/SIGTERM flush `outcome=external_kill`; tb's cap regex accepts `s`/`h`/`m` suffixes instead of misparsing `task.toml` text as seconds
- Unknown stays unknown: no invented clocks anywhere (absent/empty/malformed cap ⇒ pre-PR behavior byte-for-byte, pinned by REG tests)

### How to verify

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench -p "test_*.py"   # 402 tests
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa    -p "test_*.py"    # 101 tests
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  WF[workflows: FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC] --> CR
  KNOBS[adapter knobs from_env] --> CR[CapResolution.resolve]
  CR -->|min| RD[resolve_deadline]
  RD -->|FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS| FA[fa session clock]
  RD --> DEC[ProgressWatch / ProgressLadder]
  DEC -->|kill_at clamped to cap| KILL[cap_exceeded audit + verdict]
  RD --> AUD[audit: cap + deadline_epoch_ms]
```

</details>

`loop.remove_signal_handler(sig)` restores CPython's defaults — `SIG_DFL` (or `default_int_handler` for SIGINT) — **not** the captured `previous` (asyncio's `_UnixSelectorEventLoop.remove_signal_handler` has no notion of the prior handler). ## PR Description

Closes #1576
### What changed

The external harness cap (tb `--global-agent-timeout-sec`, harbor's per-task `[agent] timeout_sec`) is now resolved by the bench adapters and folded into ONE effective deadline — `min(external cap, adapter knobs)` — exported to fa as `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` and recorded truthfully in every audit.

### Key decisions

- `bench/fa_agent_timeout.py` owns resolution: new `CapResolution` (env scan + strict parsing; malformed caps degrade to unknown with a stderr warning) and `resolve_deadline()` as the single source of the effective cap + wrap-up deadline
- Both workflows export the cap: `bench.yml` sets `FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC` = the same number as `--global-agent-timeout-sec` (parity); `bench-harbor.yml` maps `matrix.external_cap` — the MIN of the shard tasks' declared timeouts, resolved pre-launch by `split_tasks.py`; no declared cap ⇒ no export ⇒ knobs rule alone (byte-identical)
- Deciders clamp their kill deadline to the external cap and name the winner (`external_cap`) in the verdict; audits gain `cap` resolution + `deadline_epoch_ms`, and land even on unsupervised external kills (verdict = the harness failure mode — no more bare `AGENT_STATUS_UNSET`)
- Kill-survival hardening: incremental per-sample audit checkpoints survive a SIGKILL; cancellations/SIGTERM flush `outcome=external_kill`; tb's cap regex accepts `s`/`h`/`m` suffixes instead of misparsing `task.toml` text as seconds
- Unknown stays unknown: no invented clocks anywhere (absent/empty/malformed cap ⇒ pre-PR behavior byte-for-byte, pinned by REG tests)

### How to verify

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench -p "test_*.py"   # 402 tests
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa    -p "test_*.py"    # 101 tests
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  WF[workflows: FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC] --> CR
  KNOBS[adapter knobs from_env] --> CR[CapResolution.resolve]
  CR -->|min| RD[resolve_deadline]
  RD -->|FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS| FA[fa session clock]
  RD --> DEC[ProgressWatch / ProgressLadder]
  DEC -->|kill_at clamped to cap| KILL[cap_exceeded audit + verdict]
  RD --> AUD[audit: cap + deadline_epoch_ms]
```

</details>

**1. The `finally` clobbers the process disposition instead of restoring `previous`.**
`loop.remove_signal_handler(sig)` restores CPython's defaults — `SIG_DFL` (or `default_int_handler` for SIGINT) — **not** the captured `previous` (asyncio's `_UnixSelectorEventLoop.remove_signal_handler` has no notion of the prior handler). **2. Overlapping trials clobber each other (the workflow exposes `--n-concurrent`).**
`bench-harbor.yml` takes an `n-concurrent` input (default 1, owner-raised for kimi). With >1, two FaAgent trials in one loop each call `loop.add_signal_handler(SIGTERM, ...)` — last install wins, and whichever trial finishes first strips the handler the live trial just installed. ## PR Description

Closes #1576
### What changed

The external harness cap (tb `--global-agent-timeout-sec`, harbor's per-task `[agent] timeout_sec`) is now resolved by the bench adapters and folded into ONE effective deadline — `min(external cap, adapter knobs)` — exported to fa as `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` and recorded truthfully in every audit.

### Key decisions

- `bench/fa_agent_timeout.py` owns resolution: new `CapResolution` (env scan + strict parsing; malformed caps degrade to unknown with a stderr warning) and `resolve_deadline()` as the single source of the effective cap + wrap-up deadline
- Both workflows export the cap: `bench.yml` sets `FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC` = the same number as `--global-agent-timeout-sec` (parity); `bench-harbor.yml` maps `matrix.external_cap` — the MIN of the shard tasks' declared timeouts, resolved pre-launch by `split_tasks.py`; no declared cap ⇒ no export ⇒ knobs rule alone (byte-identical)
- Deciders clamp their kill deadline to the external cap and name the winner (`external_cap`) in the verdict; audits gain `cap` resolution + `deadline_epoch_ms`, and land even on unsupervised external kills (verdict = the harness failure mode — no more bare `AGENT_STATUS_UNSET`)
- Kill-survival hardening: incremental per-sample audit checkpoints survive a SIGKILL; cancellations/SIGTERM flush `outcome=external_kill`; tb's cap regex accepts `s`/`h`/`m` suffixes instead of misparsing `task.toml` text as seconds
- Unknown stays unknown: no invented clocks anywhere (absent/empty/malformed cap ⇒ pre-PR behavior byte-for-byte, pinned by REG tests)

### How to verify

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench -p "test_*.py"   # 402 tests
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa    -p "test_*.py"    # 101 tests
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  WF[workflows: FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC] --> CR
  KNOBS[adapter knobs from_env] --> CR[CapResolution.resolve]
  CR -->|min| RD[resolve_deadline]
  RD -->|FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS| FA[fa session clock]
  RD --> DEC[ProgressWatch / ProgressLadder]
  DEC -->|kill_at clamped to cap| KILL[cap_exceeded audit + verdict]
  RD --> AUD[audit: cap + deadline_epoch_ms]
```

</details>

    async def _run_external_cap_only(self, instruction: str, environment) -> None:
        """Unsupervised exec under a known external cap (gh-1576).

        The harness owns the kill; the adapter's whole job here is I1+I2:
        fa sees the truthful deadline (via _provider_env) and every
        termination — clean exit, external cancellation, SIGTERM — leaves
        the audit record.
        """
        cap = self._cap
        self._run_environment = environment
        self._external_kill_flushed = False
        try:
            with self._kill_auditors():
                await self.exec_as_agent(
                    environment, command=self._agent_command(instruction),
                    env=self._provider_env,
                )
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            await self._flush_external_kill_audit(
                environment, None, None, cap, cause="cancelled"
            )
            raise
        await self._write_audit(
            environment, None, None, "completed",
            deadline_epoch_ms=self._deadline_epoch_ms,
            cap=cap,
        )

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1584
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1584
- **Title**: gh-1576 [GOAL] Truthful effective deadline: min(external harness cap, fa knobs) — kill the lying 3600s clock (TB 2.1 external-timeout class)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1576` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 16
- **Additions**: +2198
- **Deletions**: -203
- **Created**: 2026-10-13T10:16:37Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T21:25:26Z

## PR Description

Closes #1576
### What changed

The external harness cap (tb `--global-agent-timeout-sec`, harbor's per-task `[agent] timeout_sec`) is now resolved by the bench adapters and folded into ONE effective deadline — `min(external cap, adapter knobs)` — exported to fa as `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` and recorded truthfully in every audit.

### Key decisions

- `bench/fa_agent_timeout.py` owns resolution: new `CapResolution` (env scan + strict parsing; malformed caps degrade to unknown with a stderr warning) and `resolve_deadline()` as the single source of the effective cap + wrap-up deadline
- Both workflows export the cap: `bench.yml` sets `FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC` = the same number as `--global-agent-timeout-sec` (parity); `bench-harbor.yml` maps `matrix.external_cap` — the MIN of the shard tasks' declared timeouts, resolved pre-launch by `split_tasks.py`; no declared cap ⇒ no export ⇒ knobs rule alone (byte-identical)
- Deciders clamp their kill deadline to the external cap and name the winner (`external_cap`) in the verdict; audits gain `cap` resolution + `deadline_epoch_ms`, and land even on unsupervised external kills (verdict = the harness failure mode — no more bare `AGENT_STATUS_UNSET`)
- Kill-survival hardening: incremental per-sample audit checkpoints survive a SIGKILL; cancellations/SIGTERM flush `outcome=external_kill`; tb's cap regex accepts `s`/`h`/`m` suffixes instead of misparsing `task.toml` text as seconds
- Unknown stays unknown: no invented clocks anywhere (absent/empty/malformed cap ⇒ pre-PR behavior byte-for-byte, pinned by REG tests)

### How to verify

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench -p "test_*.py"   # 402 tests
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa    -p "test_*.py"    # 101 tests
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  WF[workflows: FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC] --> CR
  KNOBS[adapter knobs from_env] --> CR[CapResolution.resolve]
  CR -->|min| RD[resolve_deadline]
  RD -->|FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS| FA[fa session clock]
  RD --> DEC[ProgressWatch / ProgressLadder]
  DEC -->|kill_at clamped to cap| KILL[cap_exceeded audit + verdict]
  RD --> AUD[audit: cap + deadline_epoch_ms]
```

</details>

This PR's own fix taught both aggregation layers the new verdicts `external_cap` / `external_kill` (with RED→GREEN tests — the gh-1556 lesson). When no final write lands (SIGKILL of the harness process, or the cancel-path flush losing the race with container teardown and its 15s bound), the last audit on disk has `outcome: "running"`. On an `agent_timeout` row:

      "body": "⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `_kill_auditors` never restores the captured disposition, and per-trial install/remove is not concurrency-safe**

Two defects in the new signal lifecycle:

**1. The `finally` clobbers the process disposition instead of restoring `previous`.**
`loop.remove_signal_handler(sig)` restores CPython's defaults — `SIG_DFL` (or `default_int_handler` for SIGINT) — **not** the captured `previous` (asyncio's `_UnixSelectorEventLoop.remove_signal_handler` has no notion of the prior handler). So after the first supervised trial in a harbor process, the SIGTERM/SIGINT dispositions this PR found at install time are permanently gone: a later process-level SIGTERM takes the default path instead of harbor's graceful handling (the very handler the docstring says is being honored "just a few seconds later"). That flips the I2 story for anything still in flight: no graceful cancellation → no `external_kill` flushes for other trials → only `running` checkpoints survive (which the aggregation layers then misread — see the honesty-scan comment). Fix: in the `finally`, `signal.signal(sig, previous)` when `previous` is a Python-level handler (the machinery already exists — `_rehonor` does exactly this on the flush path). If `previous` is `_sighandler_noop` (harbor had its own `add_signal_handler` registration), the captured value can't restore the loop callback — in that case prefer *not installing* over half-restoring (skip when `signal.getsignal(sig)` is neither `SIG_DFL` nor `default_int_handler`).

**2. Overlapping trials clobber each other (the workflow exposes `--n-concurrent`).**
`bench-harbor.yml` takes an `n-concurrent` input (default 1, owner-raised for kimi). With >1, two FaAgent trials in one loop each call `loop.add_signal_handler(SIGTERM, ...)` — last install wins, and whichever trial finishes first strips the handler the live trial just installed. On a process SIGTERM only one trial's audit flushes; the others leave `running` checkpoints. If concurrent installs are to be supported, make the install refcounted (module-level registry keyed by signal) or document `n-concurrent=1` as a hard requirement for the SIGTERM path.

Minor: the `_rehonor` re-delivery chain is untested — every test passes `previous=None`, so the restore-and-re-kill branch (the production path) has zero coverage. A test with a real `previous` (e.g. a recording function) would pin behavior 1's fix too."

- **Title**: gh-1576 [GOAL] Truthful effective deadline: min(external harness cap, fa knobs) — kill the lying 3600s clock (TB 2.1 external-timeout class)
- **Author**: ai-teammate

- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T21:25:26Z

## PR Description

Closes #1576
### What changed

The external harness cap (tb `--global-agent-timeout-sec`, harbor's per-task `[agent] timeout_sec`) is now resolved by the bench adapters and folded into ONE effective deadline — `min(external cap, adapter knobs)` — exported to fa as `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` and recorded truthfully in every audit.

### Key decisions

- `bench/fa_agent_timeout.py` owns resolution: new `CapResolution` (env scan + strict parsing; malformed caps degrade to unknown with a stderr warning) and `resolve_deadline()` as the single source of the effective cap + wrap-up deadline
- Both workflows export the cap: `bench.yml` sets `FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC` = the same number as `--global-agent-timeout-sec` (parity); `bench-harbor.yml` maps `matrix.external_cap` — the MIN of the shard tasks' declared timeouts, resolved pre-launch by `split_tasks.py`; no declared cap ⇒ no export ⇒ knobs rule alone (byte-identical)
- Deciders clamp their kill deadline to the external cap and name the winner (`external_cap`) in the verdict; audits gain `cap` resolution + `deadline_epoch_ms`, and land even on unsupervised external kills (verdict = the harness failure mode — no more bare `AGENT_STATUS_UNSET`)
- Kill-survival hardening: incremental per-sample audit checkpoints survive a SIGKILL; cancellations/SIGTERM flush `outcome=external_kill`; tb's cap regex accepts `s`/`h`/`m` suffixes instead of misparsing `task.toml` text as seconds
- Unknown stays unknown: no invented clocks anywhere (absent/empty/malformed cap ⇒ pre-PR behavior byte-for-byte, pinned by REG tests)

### How to verify

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench -p "test_*.py"   # 402 tests
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa    -p "test_*.py"    # 101 tests
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  WF[workflows: FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC] --> CR
  KNOBS[adapter knobs from_env] --> CR[CapResolution.resolve]
  CR -->|min| RD[resolve_deadline]
  RD -->|FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS| FA[fa session clock]
  RD --> DEC[ProgressWatch / ProgressLadder]
  DEC -->|kill_at clamped to cap| KILL[cap_exceeded audit + verdict]
  RD --> AUD[audit: cap + deadline_epoch_ms]
```

</details>

    def _flush_external_kill(self, signame: str, cause: str, previous=None) -> None:
        """Write the final external_kill audit once, then honor the signal.

        Idempotent against the cancel-path flush (first writer wins).
        With a `previous` disposition (the production signal path), the
        signal is restored and re-delivered to it after the flush —
        the process still dies, the audit just outlives the race.

```python
# One process-level signal disposition per signal, shared by every live
# FaAgent trial in the loop (the workflow exposes --n-concurrent): the
# FIRST install captures the process's previous disposition, overlapping

_AUDIT_SIGNAL_HOLDER: dict = {}


def _previous_restorable(previous) -> bool:
    """False when the captured disposition cannot be restored from here.

    `signal.sighandler_noop` means another loop owns the signal via its
    own add_signal_handler registration — we can neither re-register
    their callback nor faithfully restore it, so we prefer NOT installing

    noop = getattr(signal, "sighandler_noop", None)
    return not (noop is not None and previous is noop)

            return False  # another loop owns the disposition — best-effort skip

        if agent not in entry["agents"]:

        return True

    try:
        loop.add_signal_handler(sig, _dispatch_external_kill, sig.name, loop, previous)
    except (NotImplementedError, RuntimeError, ValueError, OSError):

    _AUDIT_SIGNAL_HOLDER[sig] = {

        "previous": previous,
        "loop": loop,
        "agents": [agent],

    """Detach `agent`; the last release restores the previous disposition."""
    entry = _AUDIT_SIGNAL_HOLDER.get(sig)

        return

    except (NotImplementedError, RuntimeError, ValueError):
        pass

        except (ValueError, OSError, TypeError):

    """Sync signal-handler body: flush EVERY live trial's audit.

    Runs on the main thread at an arbitrary bytecode boundary — all loop
    interaction goes through call_soon_threadsafe. With a `previous`
    disposition (the production path), the signal is restored and
    re-delivered once every flush write has landed — the process still
    dies, the audits just outlive the race.
    """
    sig = getattr(signal, signame, None)
    entry = _AUDIT_SIGNAL_HOLDER.get(sig) if sig is not None else None
    agents = list(entry["agents"]) if entry else []

    def _flush_all() -> None:
        writes = []
        for agent in agents:
            task = agent._schedule_external_kill_write(signame, None)
            if task is not None:
                writes.append(task)

        def _rehonor(_done=None) -> None:
            if previous is None or sig is None:
                return
            try:
                signal.signal(sig, previous)
                os.kill(os.getpid(), sig)
            except (ValueError, OSError, TypeError):

        if previous is None or sig is None:
            return
        if writes:
            asyncio.gather(*writes).add_done_callback(_rehonor)
        else:

    try:
        loop.call_soon_threadsafe(_flush_all)
    except RuntimeError:
        pass  # loop already closed — nothing left to flush into
```

```python
@contextmanager
def _kill_auditors(self):
    """SIGTERM/SIGINT handlers that flush the audit before dying.

    Installed for the duration of a supervised (or external-cap-only)
    run, main thread only, and restored afterwards. The disposition is
    held PER PROCESS (module-level holder): overlapping trials attach to
    the same handler (--n-concurrent), and the captured `previous`
    disposition is restored by the LAST release — remove_signal_handler
    alone would leave SIG_DFL behind (harbor's graceful handler gone for
    the rest of the process). A disposition we cannot faithfully restore
    (another loop's add_signal_handler registration) is never stolen:
    we skip installing (the cancel-path flush still covers I2).
    """
    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
    if (
        threading.current_thread() is not threading.main_thread()
        or not hasattr(loop, "add_signal_handler")
    ):
        yield
        return
    held = []
    for sig in (signal.SIGTERM, signal.SIGINT):
        if _hold_signal_auditor(self, sig, loop):
            held.append(sig)
    try:
        yield
    finally:
        for sig in held:
            _release_signal_auditor(self, sig, loop)
```

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1584
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1584
- **Title**: gh-1576 [GOAL] Truthful effective deadline: min(external harness cap, fa knobs) — kill the lying 3600s clock (TB 2.1 external-timeout class)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1576` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 16
- **Additions**: +2198
- **Deletions**: -203
- **Created**: 2026-10-13T10:16:37Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T21:25:26Z

## PR Description

Closes #1576
### What changed

The external harness cap (tb `--global-agent-timeout-sec`, harbor's per-task `[agent] timeout_sec`) is now resolved by the bench adapters and folded into ONE effective deadline — `min(external cap, adapter knobs)` — exported to fa as `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` and recorded truthfully in every audit.

### Key decisions

- `bench/fa_agent_timeout.py` owns resolution: new `CapResolution` (env scan + strict parsing; malformed caps degrade to unknown with a stderr warning) and `resolve_deadline()` as the single source of the effective cap + wrap-up deadline
- Both workflows export the cap: `bench.yml` sets `FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC` = the same number as `--global-agent-timeout-sec` (parity); `bench-harbor.yml` maps `matrix.external_cap` — the MIN of the shard tasks' declared timeouts, resolved pre-launch by `split_tasks.py`; no declared cap ⇒ no export ⇒ knobs rule alone (byte-identical)
- Deciders clamp their kill deadline to the external cap and name the winner (`external_cap`) in the verdict; audits gain `cap` resolution + `deadline_epoch_ms`, and land even on unsupervised external kills (verdict = the harness failure mode — no more bare `AGENT_STATUS_UNSET`)
- Kill-survival hardening: incremental per-sample audit checkpoints survive a SIGKILL; cancellations/SIGTERM flush `outcome=external_kill`; tb's cap regex accepts `s`/`h`/`m` suffixes instead of misparsing `task.toml` text as seconds
- Unknown stays unknown: no invented clocks anywhere (absent/empty/malformed cap ⇒ pre-PR behavior byte-for-byte, pinned by REG tests)

### How to verify

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench -p "test_*.py"   # 402 tests
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa    -p "test_*.py"    # 101 tests
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  WF[workflows: FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC] --> CR
  KNOBS[adapter knobs from_env] --> CR[CapResolution.resolve]
  CR -->|min| RD[resolve_deadline]
  RD -->|FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS| FA[fa session clock]
  RD --> DEC[ProgressWatch / ProgressLadder]
  DEC -->|kill_at clamped to cap| KILL[cap_exceeded audit + verdict]
  RD --> AUD[audit: cap + deadline_epoch_ms]
```

</details>

**1. The `finally` clobbers the process disposition instead of restoring `previous`.**
`loop.remove_signal_handler(sig)` restores CPython's defaults — `SIG_DFL` (or `default_int_handler` for SIGINT) — **not** the captured `previous` (asyncio's `_UnixSelectorEventLoop.remove_signal_handler` has no notion of the prior handler). With >1, two FaAgent trials in one loop each call `loop.add_signal_handler(SIGTERM, ...)` — last install wins, and whichever trial finishes first strips the handler the live trial just installed.         With a `previous` disposition (the production signal path), the
        signal is restored and re-delivered to it after the flush —
        the process still dies, the audit just outlives the race.

## PR Description

Closes #1576
### What changed

The external harness cap (tb `--global-agent-timeout-sec`, harbor's per-task `[agent] timeout_sec`) is now resolved by the bench adapters and folded into ONE effective deadline — `min(external cap, adapter knobs)` — exported to fa as `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` and recorded truthfully in every audit.

### Key decisions

- `bench/fa_agent_timeout.py` owns resolution: new `CapResolution` (env scan + strict parsing; malformed caps degrade to unknown with a stderr warning) and `resolve_deadline()` as the single source of the effective cap + wrap-up deadline
- Both workflows export the cap: `bench.yml` sets `FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC` = the same number as `--global-agent-timeout-sec` (parity); `bench-harbor.yml` maps `matrix.external_cap` — the MIN of the shard tasks' declared timeouts, resolved pre-launch by `split_tasks.py`; no declared cap ⇒ no export ⇒ knobs rule alone (byte-identical)
- Deciders clamp their kill deadline to the external cap and name the winner (`external_cap`) in the verdict; audits gain `cap` resolution + `deadline_epoch_ms`, and land even on unsupervised external kills (verdict = the harness failure mode — no more bare `AGENT_STATUS_UNSET`)
- Kill-survival hardening: incremental per-sample audit checkpoints survive a SIGKILL; cancellations/SIGTERM flush `outcome=external_kill`; tb's cap regex accepts `s`/`h`/`m` suffixes instead of misparsing `task.toml` text as seconds
- Unknown stays unknown: no invented clocks anywhere (absent/empty/malformed cap ⇒ pre-PR behavior byte-for-byte, pinned by REG tests)

### How to verify

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench -p "test_*.py"   # 402 tests
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa    -p "test_*.py"    # 101 tests
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  WF[workflows: FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC] --> CR
  KNOBS[adapter knobs from_env] --> CR[CapResolution.resolve]
  CR -->|min| RD[resolve_deadline]
  RD -->|FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS| FA[fa session clock]
  RD --> DEC[ProgressWatch / ProgressLadder]
  DEC -->|kill_at clamped to cap| KILL[cap_exceeded audit + verdict]
  RD --> AUD[audit: cap + deadline_epoch_ms]
```

</details>

    async def _run_external_cap_only(self, instruction: str, environment) -> None:
        """Unsupervised exec under a known external cap (gh-1576).

        The harness owns the kill; the adapter's whole job here is I1+I2:
        fa sees the truthful deadline (via _provider_env) and every
        termination — clean exit, external cancellation, SIGTERM — leaves
        the audit record.
        """
        cap = self._cap
        self._run_environment = environment
        self._external_kill_flushed = False
        try:
            with self._kill_auditors():
                await self.exec_as_agent(
                    environment, command=self._agent_command(instruction),
                    env=self._provider_env,
                )
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            await self._flush_external_kill_audit(
                environment, None, None, cap, cause="cancelled"
            )
            raise
        await self._write_audit(
            environment, None, None, "completed",
            deadline_epoch_ms=self._deadline_epoch_ms,
            cap=cap,
        )

    # ── gh-1576: external-kill audit trail (I2) ──────────────────────────

    @contextmanager
    def _kill_auditors(self):
        """SIGTERM/SIGINT handlers that flush the audit before dying.

        Installed for the duration of a supervised (or external-cap-only)
        run, main thread only, and restored afterwards — harbor's own
        handlers (e.g. jobs.py's SIGTERM→KeyboardInterrupt) are captured
        and re-delivered once the flush lands, so termination semantics

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1584
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1584
- **Title**: gh-1576 [GOAL] Truthful effective deadline: min(external harness cap, fa knobs) — kill the lying 3600s clock (TB 2.1 external-timeout class)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1576` → `main`

- **Deletions**: -203
- **Created**: 2026-10-13T10:16:37Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T21:25:26Z

## PR Description

Closes #1576
### What changed

The external harness cap (tb `--global-agent-timeout-sec`, harbor's per-task `[agent] timeout_sec`) is now resolved by the bench adapters and folded into ONE effective deadline — `min(external cap, adapter knobs)` — exported to fa as `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` and recorded truthfully in every audit.

### Key decisions

- `bench/fa_agent_timeout.py` owns resolution: new `CapResolution` (env scan + strict parsing; malformed caps degrade to unknown with a stderr warning) and `resolve_deadline()` as the single source of the effective cap + wrap-up deadline
- Both workflows export the cap: `bench.yml` sets `FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC` = the same number as `--global-agent-timeout-sec` (parity); `bench-harbor.yml` maps `matrix.external_cap` — the MIN of the shard tasks' declared timeouts, resolved pre-launch by `split_tasks.py`; no declared cap ⇒ no export ⇒ knobs rule alone (byte-identical)
- Deciders clamp their kill deadline to the external cap and name the winner (`external_cap`) in the verdict; audits gain `cap` resolution + `deadline_epoch_ms`, and land even on unsupervised external kills (verdict = the harness failure mode — no more bare `AGENT_STATUS_UNSET`)
- Kill-survival hardening: incremental per-sample audit checkpoints survive a SIGKILL; cancellations/SIGTERM flush `outcome=external_kill`; tb's cap regex accepts `s`/`h`/`m` suffixes instead of misparsing `task.toml` text as seconds
- Unknown stays unknown: no invented clocks anywhere (absent/empty/malformed cap ⇒ pre-PR behavior byte-for-byte, pinned by REG tests)

### How to verify

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench -p "test_*.py"   # 402 tests
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa    -p "test_*.py"    # 101 tests
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  WF[workflows: FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC] --> CR
  KNOBS[adapter knobs from_env] --> CR[CapResolution.resolve]
  CR -->|min| RD[resolve_deadline]
  RD -->|FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS| FA[fa session clock]
  RD --> DEC[ProgressWatch / ProgressLadder]
  DEC -->|kill_at clamped to cap| KILL[cap_exceeded audit + verdict]
  RD --> AUD[audit: cap + deadline_epoch_ms]
```

</details>

Two defects in the new signal lifecycle:

**1. The `finally` clobbers the process disposition instead of restoring `previous`.**
`loop.remove_signal_handler(sig)` restores CPython's defaults — `SIG_DFL` (or `default_int_handler` for SIGINT) — **not** the captured `previous` (asyncio's `_UnixSelectorEventLoop.remove_signal_handler` has no notion of the prior handler). `bench-harbor.yml` takes an `n-concurrent` input (default 1, owner-raised for kimi). With >1, two FaAgent trials in one loop each call `loop.add_signal_handler(SIGTERM, ...)` — last install wins, and whichever trial finishes first strips the handler the live trial just installed. On a process SIGTERM only one trial's audit flushes; the others leave `running` checkpoints. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1584
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1584
- **Title**: gh-1576 [GOAL] Truthful effective deadline: min(external harness cap, fa knobs) — kill the lying 3600s clock (TB 2.1 external-timeout class)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1576` → `main`

- **Additions**: +2198
- **Deletions**: -203
- **Created**: 2026-10-13T10:16:37Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T21:25:26Z

## PR Description

Closes #1576
### What changed

The external harness cap (tb `--global-agent-timeout-sec`, harbor's per-task `[agent] timeout_sec`) is now resolved by the bench adapters and folded into ONE effective deadline — `min(external cap, adapter knobs)` — exported to fa as `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` and recorded truthfully in every audit.

### Key decisions

- `bench/fa_agent_timeout.py` owns resolution: new `CapResolution` (env scan + strict parsing; malformed caps degrade to unknown with a stderr warning) and `resolve_deadline()` as the single source of the effective cap + wrap-up deadline
- Both workflows export the cap: `bench.yml` sets `FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC` = the same number as `--global-agent-timeout-sec` (parity); `bench-harbor.yml` maps `matrix.external_cap` — the MIN of the shard tasks' declared timeouts, resolved pre-launch by `split_tasks.py`; no declared cap ⇒ no export ⇒ knobs rule alone (byte-identical)
- Deciders clamp their kill deadline to the external cap and name the winner (`external_cap`) in the verdict; audits gain `cap` resolution + `deadline_epoch_ms`, and land even on unsupervised external kills (verdict = the harness failure mode — no more bare `AGENT_STATUS_UNSET`)
- Kill-survival hardening: incremental per-sample audit checkpoints survive a SIGKILL; cancellations/SIGTERM flush `outcome=external_kill`; tb's cap regex accepts `s`/`h`/`m` suffixes instead of misparsing `task.toml` text as seconds
- Unknown stays unknown: no invented clocks anywhere (absent/empty/malformed cap ⇒ pre-PR behavior byte-for-byte, pinned by REG tests)

### How to verify

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench -p "test_*.py"   # 402 tests
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa    -p "test_*.py"    # 101 tests
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  WF[workflows: FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC] --> CR
  KNOBS[adapter knobs from_env] --> CR[CapResolution.resolve]
  CR -->|min| RD[resolve_deadline]
  RD -->|FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS| FA[fa session clock]
  RD --> DEC[ProgressWatch / ProgressLadder]
  DEC -->|kill_at clamped to cap| KILL[cap_exceeded audit + verdict]
  RD --> AUD[audit: cap + deadline_epoch_ms]
```

</details>

Interesting: there's a commit `5977e2678 gh-1576 rework: the post-mortem honesty scan honors the cap verdicts too` — that's not mine! My commit was `147d883 gh-1576 rework: name the cap verdicts truthfully everywhere`. Someone else (a parallel rework leg?) also fixed the honesty scan. Then two merges of main brought the tree to 1b21aad (current HEAD).

`loop.remove_signal_handler(sig)` restores CPython's defaults — `SIG_DFL` (or `default_int_handler` for SIGINT) — **not** the captured `previous` (asyncio's `_UnixSelectorEventLoop.remove_signal_handler` has no notion of the prior handler). With >1, two FaAgent trials in one loop each call `loop.add_signal_handler(SIGTERM, ...)` — last install wins, and whichever trial finishes first strips the handler the live trial just installed. ## PR Description

Closes #1576
### What changed

The external harness cap (tb `--global-agent-timeout-sec`, harbor's per-task `[agent] timeout_sec`) is now resolved by the bench adapters and folded into ONE effective deadline — `min(external cap, adapter knobs)` — exported to fa as `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` and recorded truthfully in every audit.

### Key decisions

- `bench/fa_agent_timeout.py` owns resolution: new `CapResolution` (env scan + strict parsing; malformed caps degrade to unknown with a stderr warning) and `resolve_deadline()` as the single source of the effective cap + wrap-up deadline
- Both workflows export the cap: `bench.yml` sets `FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC` = the same number as `--global-agent-timeout-sec` (parity); `bench-harbor.yml` maps `matrix.external_cap` — the MIN of the shard tasks' declared timeouts, resolved pre-launch by `split_tasks.py`; no declared cap ⇒ no export ⇒ knobs rule alone (byte-identical)
- Deciders clamp their kill deadline to the external cap and name the winner (`external_cap`) in the verdict; audits gain `cap` resolution + `deadline_epoch_ms`, and land even on unsupervised external kills (verdict = the harness failure mode — no more bare `AGENT_STATUS_UNSET`)
- Kill-survival hardening: incremental per-sample audit checkpoints survive a SIGKILL; cancellations/SIGTERM flush `outcome=external_kill`; tb's cap regex accepts `s`/`h`/`m` suffixes instead of misparsing `task.toml` text as seconds
- Unknown stays unknown: no invented clocks anywhere (absent/empty/malformed cap ⇒ pre-PR behavior byte-for-byte, pinned by REG tests)

### How to verify

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench -p "test_*.py"   # 402 tests
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa    -p "test_*.py"    # 101 tests
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  WF[workflows: FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC] --> CR
  KNOBS[adapter knobs from_env] --> CR[CapResolution.resolve]
  CR -->|min| RD[resolve_deadline]
  RD -->|FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS| FA[fa session clock]
  RD --> DEC[ProgressWatch / ProgressLadder]
  DEC -->|kill_at clamped to cap| KILL[cap_exceeded audit + verdict]
  RD --> AUD[audit: cap + deadline_epoch_ms]
```

</details>

Two defects in the new signal lifecycle:

**1. The `finally` clobbers the process disposition instead of restoring `previous`.**
`loop.remove_signal_handler(sig)` restores CPython's defaults — `SIG_DFL` (or `default_int_handler` for SIGINT) — **not** the captured `previous` (asyncio's `_UnixSelectorEventLoop.remove_signal_handler` has no notion of the prior handler). So after the first supervised trial in a harbor process, the SIGTERM/SIGINT dispositions this PR found at install time are permanently gone: a later process-level SIGTERM takes the default path instead of harbor's graceful handling (the very handler the docstring says is being honored "just a few seconds later"). That flips the I2 story for anything still in flight: no graceful cancellation → no `external_kill` flushes for other trials → only `running` checkpoints survive (which the aggregation layers then misread — see the honesty-scan comment). Fix: in the `finally`, `signal.signal(sig, previous)` when `previous` is a Python-level handler (the machinery already exists — `_rehonor` does exactly this on the flush path). If `previous` is `_sighandler_noop` (harbor had its own `add_signal_handler` registration), the captured value can't restore the loop callback — in that case prefer *not installing* over half-restoring (skip when `signal.getsignal(sig)` is neither `SIG_DFL` nor `default_int_handler`).

**2. Overlapping trials clobber each other (the workflow exposes `--n-concurrent`).**
`bench-harbor.yml` takes an `n-concurrent` input (default 1, owner-raised for kimi). With >1, two FaAgent trials in one loop each call `loop.add_signal_handler(SIGTERM, ...)` — last install wins, and whichever trial finishes first strips the handler the live trial just installed. On a process SIGTERM only one trial's audit flushes; the others leave `running` checkpoints. If concurrent installs are to be supported, make the install refcounted (module-level registry keyed by signal) or document `n-concurrent=1` as a hard requirement for the SIGTERM path.

Minor: the `_rehonor` re-delivery chain is untested — every test passes `previous=None`, so the restore-and-re-kill branch (the production path) has zero coverage. A test with a real `previous` (e.g. a recording function) would pin behavior 1's fix too."

def _dart_duration_seconds(declaration: str) -> float:
    """Seconds inside a Dart `Duration(...)` constructor call.

    Accepts any argument subset/order (`Duration(seconds: 180)`,
    `Duration(minutes: 5)`, `Duration(minutes: 1, seconds: 30)`,
    `Duration(milliseconds: 500)`) — the coupling REG (gh-1430) feeds it
    the `providerStreamIdleTimeout` line from the Dart source, and the
    parse must survive a benign unit change there.
    """
    body = declaration[declaration.index("(") + 1 : declaration.rindex(")")]
    factors = {
        "milliseconds": 0.001,
        "seconds": 1.0,
        "minutes": 60.0,
        "hours": 3600.0,
    }
    total = 0.0
    matched = False
    for name, factor in factors.items():

        # `milliseconds`, and a bare substring match would double-count
        # every milliseconds argument as whole seconds (gh-1430 review).
        for value in re.findall(rf"\b{name}\s*:\s*([0-9.]+)", body):
            matched = True
            total += float(value) * factor
    if not matched:
        raise ValueError(f"no Duration arguments in: {declaration!r}")
    return total

## PR Description

Closes #1576
### What changed

The external harness cap (tb `--global-agent-timeout-sec`, harbor's per-task `[agent] timeout_sec`) is now resolved by the bench adapters and folded into ONE effective deadline — `min(external cap, adapter knobs)` — exported to fa as `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` and recorded truthfully in every audit.

### Key decisions

- `bench/fa_agent_timeout.py` owns resolution: new `CapResolution` (env scan + strict parsing; malformed caps degrade to unknown with a stderr warning) and `resolve_deadline()` as the single source of the effective cap + wrap-up deadline
- Both workflows export the cap: `bench.yml` sets `FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC` = the same number as `--global-agent-timeout-sec` (parity); `bench-harbor.yml` maps `matrix.external_cap` — the MIN of the shard tasks' declared timeouts, resolved pre-launch by `split_tasks.py`; no declared cap ⇒ no export ⇒ knobs rule alone (byte-identical)
- Deciders clamp their kill deadline to the external cap and name the winner (`external_cap`) in the verdict; audits gain `cap` resolution + `deadline_epoch_ms`, and land even on unsupervised external kills (verdict = the harness failure mode — no more bare `AGENT_STATUS_UNSET`)
- Kill-survival hardening: incremental per-sample audit checkpoints survive a SIGKILL; cancellations/SIGTERM flush `outcome=external_kill`; tb's cap regex accepts `s`/`h`/`m` suffixes instead of misparsing `task.toml` text as seconds
- Unknown stays unknown: no invented clocks anywhere (absent/empty/malformed cap ⇒ pre-PR behavior byte-for-byte, pinned by REG tests)

### How to verify

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench -p "test_*.py"   # 402 tests
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa    -p "test_*.py"    # 101 tests
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  WF[workflows: FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC] --> CR
  KNOBS[adapter knobs from_env] --> CR[CapResolution.resolve]
  CR -->|min| RD[resolve_deadline]
  RD -->|FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS| FA[fa session clock]
  RD --> DEC[ProgressWatch / ProgressLadder]
  DEC -->|kill_at clamped to cap| KILL[cap_exceeded audit + verdict]
  RD --> AUD[audit: cap + deadline_epoch_ms]
```

</details>

      "body": "⚠️ **IMPORTANT: new audit outcomes `running` / raw failure-modes are missing from the honesty-justified set — the gh-1556 lesson, one outcome short**

This PR's own fix taught both aggregation layers the new verdicts `external_cap` / `external_kill` (with RED→GREEN tests — the gh-1556 lesson). But the PR also introduces two more terminal audit outcome values that both `_AUDIT_JUSTIFIED` sets (`bench/terminal_bench/summary.py:260` and `bench/post_mortem_usage.py:140` — "change both together" per their comments) do not know:

1. **`running`** — the incremental checkpoints (`_maybe_checkpoint` in `bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py`, the poll-loop checkpoint in `bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py`) are explicitly designed as the best-effort residue a SIGKILL leaves behind (E3). When no final write lands (SIGKILL of the harness process, or the cancel-path flush losing the race with container teardown and its 15s bound), the last audit on disk has `outcome: "running"`. On an `agent_timeout` row:
   - `summary._score_honesty` sees the audit, `outcome` not justified → **unconditional contradiction** (the legacy gap fallback is skipped when an audit exists — summary.py's `contradictions.append(row.trial)` path);
   - `post_mortem._audit_justified` → False → the gap scan runs → a progressing trial (exactly the incident shape) reports a false `SCORE HONESTY VIOLATION`.
   Both layers would blame the bench for a kill its decider never made — the checkpoint truthfully says "no verdict yet".

2. **Raw failure-mode strings from the tb stock path** — `bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py` (knobs=None, cap known) writes `str(result.failure_mode.value)` as the outcome (e.g. `"agent_timeout"` for a harness-timeout kill). That value is likewise absent from both sets → same unconditional-contradiction behavior, even for a legitimately stalled trial whose big gaps would have cleared the legacy scan had no audit existed.

Suggested fix (one of):
- add `"running"` to both justified sets (it names no bench kill, so it cannot be a bench contradiction) and either add the failure-mode vocabulary or normalize the tb stock-path writer to emit a recognized verdict (e.g. map a harness timeout to `external_kill` — the kill did come from outside the adapter);
- or, in the scanners, treat an audit whose `checkpoint` flag is set as "no verdict" and fall through to the legacy gap scan instead of asserting a contradiction.

Also worth a RED→GREEN test per layer, mirroring `test_external_cap_kill_is_a_justified_audit_outcome`."

      "body": "⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `_kill_auditors` never restores the captured disposition, and per-trial install/remove is not concurrency-safe**

Two defects in the new signal lifecycle:

**1. The `finally` clobbers the process disposition instead of restoring `previous`.**
`loop.remove_signal_handler(sig)` restores CPython's defaults — `SIG_DFL` (or `default_int_handler` for SIGINT) — **not** the captured `previous` (asyncio's `_UnixSelectorEventLoop.remove_signal_handler` has no notion of the prior handler). So after the first supervised trial in a harbor process, the SIGTERM/SIGINT dispositions this PR found at install time are permanently gone: a later process-level SIGTERM takes the default path instead of harbor's graceful handling (the very handler the docstring says is being honored "just a few seconds later"). That flips the I2 story for anything still in flight: no graceful cancellation → no `external_kill` flushes for other trials → only `running` checkpoints survive (which the aggregation layers then misread — see the honesty-scan comment). Fix: in the `finally`, `signal.signal(sig, previous)` when `previous` is a Python-level handler (the machinery already exists — `_rehonor` does exactly this on the flush path). If `previous` is `_sighandler_noop` (harbor had its own `add_signal_handler` registration), the captured value can't restore the loop callback — in that case prefer *not installing* over half-restoring (skip when `signal.getsignal(sig)` is neither `SIG_DFL` nor `default_int_handler`).

**2. Overlapping trials clobber each other (the workflow exposes `--n-concurrent`).**
`bench-harbor.yml` takes an `n-concurrent` input (default 1, owner-raised for kimi). With >1, two FaAgent trials in one loop each call `loop.add_signal_handler(SIGTERM, ...)` — last install wins, and whichever trial finishes first strips the handler the live trial just installed. On a process SIGTERM only one trial's audit flushes; the others leave `running` checkpoints. If concurrent installs are to be supported, make the install refcounted (module-level registry keyed by signal) or document `n-concurrent=1` as a hard requirement for the SIGTERM path.

Minor: the `_rehonor` re-delivery chain is untested — every test passes `previous=None`, so the restore-and-re-kill branch (the production path) has zero coverage. A test with a real `previous` (e.g. a recording function) would pin behavior 1's fix too."

```python
    "crashed" if error is not None else "completed",
    deadline_epoch_ms=self._deadline_epoch_ms,
    cap=cap,

```

        With a `previous` disposition (the production signal path), the
        signal is restored and re-delivered to it after the flush —
        the process still dies, the audit just outlives the race.

    """Seconds inside a Dart `Duration(...)` constructor call.

- **Title**: gh-1576 [GOAL] Truthful effective deadline: min(external harness cap, fa knobs) — kill the lying 3600s clock (TB 2.1 external-timeout class)

## PR Description

Closes #1576
### What changed

The external harness cap (tb `--global-agent-timeout-sec`, harbor's per-task `[agent] timeout_sec`) is now resolved by the bench adapters and folded into ONE effective deadline — `min(external cap, adapter knobs)` — exported to fa as `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` and recorded truthfully in every audit.

### Key decisions

- `bench/fa_agent_timeout.py` owns resolution: new `CapResolution` (env scan + strict parsing; malformed caps degrade to unknown with a stderr warning) and `resolve_deadline()` as the single source of the effective cap + wrap-up deadline
- Both workflows export the cap: `bench.yml` sets `FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC` = the same number as `--global-agent-timeout-sec` (parity); `bench-harbor.yml` maps `matrix.external_cap` — the MIN of the shard tasks' declared timeouts, resolved pre-launch by `split_tasks.py`; no declared cap ⇒ no export ⇒ knobs rule alone (byte-identical)
- Deciders clamp their kill deadline to the external cap and name the winner (`external_cap`) in the verdict; audits gain `cap` resolution + `deadline_epoch_ms`, and land even on unsupervised external kills (verdict = the harness failure mode — no more bare `AGENT_STATUS_UNSET`)
- Kill-survival hardening: incremental per-sample audit checkpoints survive a SIGKILL; cancellations/SIGTERM flush `outcome=external_kill`; tb's cap regex accepts `s`/`h`/`m` suffixes instead of misparsing `task.toml` text as seconds
- Unknown stays unknown: no invented clocks anywhere (absent/empty/malformed cap ⇒ pre-PR behavior byte-for-byte, pinned by REG tests)

### How to verify

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench -p "test_*.py"   # 402 tests
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa    -p "test_*.py"    # 101 tests
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  WF[workflows: FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC] --> CR
  KNOBS[adapter knobs from_env] --> CR[CapResolution.resolve]
  CR -->|min| RD[resolve_deadline]
  RD -->|FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS| FA[fa session clock]
  RD --> DEC[ProgressWatch / ProgressLadder]
  DEC -->|kill_at clamped to cap| KILL[cap_exceeded audit + verdict]
  RD --> AUD[audit: cap + deadline_epoch_ms]
```

</details>

With >1, two FaAgent trials in one loop each call `loop.add_signal_handler(SIGTERM, ...)` — last install wins, and whichever trial finishes first strips the handler the live trial just installed.     def _flush_external_kill(self, signame: str, cause: str, previous=None) -> None:
        """Write the final external_kill audit once, then honor the signal.

        Idempotent against the cancel-path flush (first writer wins).
        With a `previous` disposition (the production signal path), the
        signal is restored and re-delivered to it after the flush —
        the process still dies, the audit just outlives the race.

        if getattr(self, "_external_kill_flushed", False):

        self._external_kill_flushed = True
        environment = getattr(self, "_run_environment", None)

Run: python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench
The adapter-level tests skip when terminal_bench / harbor is not installed;
the ladder tests run anywhere (pure stdlib shared module).

import asyncio
import base64

import warnings

import fa_agent_timeout
from fa_agent_timeout import ProgressLadder, TimeoutKnobs, audit_dict

def _importable(name: str) -> bool:
    # find_spec is not enough: with bench/terminal_bench on sys.path (as
    # unittest discover does), find_spec("terminal_bench") matches the
    # DIRECTORY itself as a namespace package and false-positives.
    try:
        module = importlib.import_module(name)
    except ImportError:
        return False
    # test_progress_watch_adapter installs a stdlib stub package under the
    # same name (so its ITs run where terminal-bench is not installed);
    # a stub is not the real dependency.
    return not getattr(module, "__fa_tb_stub__", False)


TB_AVAILABLE = _importable("terminal_bench.agents.base_agent")
HARBOR_AVAILABLE = _importable("harbor")

KNOB_NAMES = (
    "FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC",
    "FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION",
    "FA_AGENT_IDLE_WINDOW_SEC",
    "FA_AGENT_CEILING_MULTIPLIER",
)

# gh-1576: the external harness cap rides its own env var; every clean-env
# helper must strip it so a host-exported cap cannot leak into a test that
# means to pin the no-cap byte-identity.
EXTERNAL_CAP_NAME = "FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC"


def clean_env(**overrides):
    env = {
        name: value
        for name, value in os.environ.items()
        if name not in KNOB_NAMES + (EXTERNAL_CAP_NAME,)
    }
    env.update(overrides)
    return env


def _dart_duration_seconds(declaration: str) -> float:
    """Seconds inside a Dart `Duration(...)` constructor call.

    Accepts any argument subset/order (`Duration(seconds: 180)`,
    `Duration(minutes: 5)`, `Duration(minutes: 1, seconds: 30)`,
    `Duration(milliseconds: 500)`) — the coupling REG (gh-1430) feeds it
    the `providerStreamIdleTimeout` line from the Dart source, and the
    parse must survive a benign unit change there.
    """
    body = declaration[declaration.index("(") + 1 : declaration.rindex(")")]
    factors = {
        "milliseconds": 0.001,
        "seconds": 1.0,
        "minutes": 60.0,
        "hours": 3600.0,
    }
    total = 0.0
    matched = False
    for name, factor in factors.items():
        # \b anchors the unit name: `seconds` occurs inside
        # `milliseconds`, and a bare substring match would double-count
        # every milliseconds argument as whole seconds (gh-1430 review).
        for value in re.findall(rf"\b{name}\s*:\s*([0-9.]+)", body):
            matched = True
            total += float(value) * factor
    if not matched:
        raise ValueError(f"no Duration arguments in: {declaration!r}")
    return total

class DartDurationParseTest(unittest.TestCase):
    """Unit table for _dart_duration_seconds (gh-1430 review thread 1).

    The coupling REG feeds this helper the `providerStreamIdleTimeout`
    line straight from the Dart source, and the docstring promises the
    parse survives a benign unit change there. `seconds` occurs INSIDE
    `milliseconds`, so the unit match must be word-boundary anchored —

class TerminalBenchExternalCapTest(unittest.TestCase):
    """IT-4 (gh-1576): the same cap contract through the tb adapter.

    The tb harness cap (its --global-agent-timeout-sec / dataset caps) is
    normally the LARGER clock (bench.yml pins it above the adapter's own
    ceiling), so the external cap must be inert there (E4) — but when a
    harness ever caps BELOW the knobs (the harbor incident shape), the
    launch line, the audit, and the decider must all follow the smaller
    truth. Parity surface: identical audit schema to the harbor adapter.
    """

    def setUp(self):
        self.tmpdir = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.tmpdir.cleanup)
        root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
        spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
            "legacy_fa_agent_extcap", root / "terminal_bench" / "fa_agent.py"
        )
        self.legacy_fa = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
        spec.loader.exec_module(self.legacy_fa)

    def _agent(self):
        tarball = Path(self.tmpdir.name) / "fa-bundle.tar.gz"
        tarball.write_bytes(b"")
        with mock.patch.dict(os.environ, {"FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL": str(tarball)}):
            return self.legacy_fa.FaAgent()

    def _run_supervised(self, env_overrides, stock, logging_dir):
        agent = self._agent()
        session = FakeTmuxSession()
        env = clean_env_all(
            FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION="1",
            FA_STALL_GAP_SEC="360",
            FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC="3600",
            FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG="{}",
            **env_overrides,
        )
        with mock.patch.dict(os.environ, env), mock.patch.object(
            self.legacy_fa, "_POLL_SEC", 0.05
        ), mock.patch.object(
            self.legacy_fa.AbstractInstalledAgent, "perform_task",
            side_effect=stock,
        ):
            started = time.monotonic()
            agent.perform_task("instr", session, logging_dir)

- **Doc drift (Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6sAK15`, blocking):** `AGENTS.md` and `.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml` promised a `cap_exceeded` verdict; the code emits two distinct, test-pinned names — `external_cap` (the decider's kill at the binding external cap) and `external_kill` (the flush for a kill arriving from outside: harbor's `wait_for` cancellation / SIGTERM). # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1584
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1584
- **Title**: gh-1576 [GOAL] Truthful effective deadline: min(external harness cap, fa knobs) — kill the lying 3600s clock (TB 2.1 external-timeout class)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1576` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 16
- **Additions**: +2198
- **Deletions**: -203
- **Created**: 2026-10-13T10:16:37Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T21:25:26Z

## PR Description

Closes #1576
### What changed

The external harness cap (tb `--global-agent-timeout-sec`, harbor's per-task `[agent] timeout_sec`) is now resolved by the bench adapters and folded into ONE effective deadline — `min(external cap, adapter knobs)` — exported to fa as `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` and recorded truthfully in every audit.

### Key decisions

- `bench/fa_agent_timeout.py` owns resolution: new `CapResolution` (env scan + strict parsing; malformed caps degrade to unknown with a stderr warning) and `resolve_deadline()` as the single source of the effective cap + wrap-up deadline
- Both workflows export the cap: `bench.yml` sets `FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC` = the same number as `--global-agent-timeout-sec` (parity); `bench-harbor.yml` maps `matrix.external_cap` — the MIN of the shard tasks' declared timeouts, resolved pre-launch by `split_tasks.py`; no declared cap ⇒ no export ⇒ knobs rule alone (byte-identical)
- Deciders clamp their kill deadline to the external cap and name the winner (`external_cap`) in the verdict; audits gain `cap` resolution + `deadline_epoch_ms`, and land even on unsupervised external kills (verdict = the harness failure mode — no more bare `AGENT_STATUS_UNSET`)
- Kill-survival hardening: incremental per-sample audit checkpoints survive a SIGKILL; cancellations/SIGTERM flush `outcome=external_kill`; tb's cap regex accepts `s`/`h`/`m` suffixes instead of misparsing `task.toml` text as seconds
- Unknown stays unknown: no invented clocks anywhere (absent/empty/malformed cap ⇒ pre-PR behavior byte-for-byte, pinned by REG tests)

### How to verify

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench -p "test_*.py"   # 402 tests
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa    -p "test_*.py"    # 101 tests
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  WF[workflows: FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC] --> CR
  KNOBS[adapter knobs from_env] --> CR[CapResolution.resolve]
  CR -->|min| RD[resolve_deadline]
  RD -->|FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS| FA[fa session clock]
  RD --> DEC[ProgressWatch / ProgressLadder]
  DEC -->|kill_at clamped to cap| KILL[cap_exceeded audit + verdict]
  RD --> AUD[audit: cap + deadline_epoch_ms]
```

</details>

Interesting: there's a commit `5977e2678 gh-1576 rework: the post-mortem honesty scan honors the cap verdicts too` — that's not mine! My commit was `147d883 gh-1576 rework: name the cap verdicts truthfully everywhere`. Someone else (a parallel rework leg?) also fixed the honesty scan. Then two merges of main brought the tree to 1b21aad (current HEAD).

Two defects in the new signal lifecycle:

**1. The `finally` clobbers the process disposition instead of restoring `previous`.**
`loop.remove_signal_handler(sig)` restores CPython's defaults — `SIG_DFL` (or `default_int_handler` for SIGINT) — **not** the captured `previous` (asyncio's `_UnixSelectorEventLoop.remove_signal_handler` has no notion of the prior handler). **2. Overlapping trials clobber each other (the workflow exposes `--n-concurrent`).**
`bench-harbor.yml` takes an `n-concurrent` input (default 1, owner-raised for kimi). With >1, two FaAgent trials in one loop each call `loop.add_signal_handler(SIGTERM, ...)` — last install wins, and whichever trial finishes first strips the handler the live trial just installed. On a process SIGTERM only one trial's audit flushes; the others leave `running` checkpoints. def _dart_duration_seconds(declaration: str) -> float:
    """Seconds inside a Dart `Duration(...)` constructor call.

    Accepts any argument subset/order (`Duration(seconds: 180)`,
    `Duration(minutes: 5)`, `Duration(minutes: 1, seconds: 30)`,
    `Duration(milliseconds: 500)`) — the coupling REG (gh-1430) feeds it
    the `providerStreamIdleTimeout` line from the Dart source, and the
    parse must survive a benign unit change there.
    """
    body = declaration[declaration.index("(") + 1 : declaration.rindex(")")]
    factors = {
        "milliseconds": 0.001,
        "seconds": 1.0,
        "minutes": 60.0,
        "hours": 3600.0,
    }
    total = 0.0
    matched = False
    for name, factor in factors.items():
        # \b anchors the unit name: `seconds` occurs inside
        # `milliseconds`, and a bare substring match would double-count
        # every milliseconds argument as whole seconds (gh-1430 review).
        for value in re.findall(rf"\b{name}\s*:\s*([0-9.]+)", body):

            total += float(value) * factor

        raise ValueError(f"no Duration arguments in: {declaration!r}")
    return total

- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T21:25:26Z

## PR Description

Closes #1576
### What changed

The external harness cap (tb `--global-agent-timeout-sec`, harbor's per-task `[agent] timeout_sec`) is now resolved by the bench adapters and folded into ONE effective deadline — `min(external cap, adapter knobs)` — exported to fa as `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` and recorded truthfully in every audit.

### Key decisions

- `bench/fa_agent_timeout.py` owns resolution: new `CapResolution` (env scan + strict parsing; malformed caps degrade to unknown with a stderr warning) and `resolve_deadline()` as the single source of the effective cap + wrap-up deadline
- Both workflows export the cap: `bench.yml` sets `FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC` = the same number as `--global-agent-timeout-sec` (parity); `bench-harbor.yml` maps `matrix.external_cap` — the MIN of the shard tasks' declared timeouts, resolved pre-launch by `split_tasks.py`; no declared cap ⇒ no export ⇒ knobs rule alone (byte-identical)
- Deciders clamp their kill deadline to the external cap and name the winner (`external_cap`) in the verdict; audits gain `cap` resolution + `deadline_epoch_ms`, and land even on unsupervised external kills (verdict = the harness failure mode — no more bare `AGENT_STATUS_UNSET`)
- Kill-survival hardening: incremental per-sample audit checkpoints survive a SIGKILL; cancellations/SIGTERM flush `outcome=external_kill`; tb's cap regex accepts `s`/`h`/`m` suffixes instead of misparsing `task.toml` text as seconds
- Unknown stays unknown: no invented clocks anywhere (absent/empty/malformed cap ⇒ pre-PR behavior byte-for-byte, pinned by REG tests)

### How to verify

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench -p "test_*.py"   # 402 tests
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa    -p "test_*.py"    # 101 tests
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  WF[workflows: FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC] --> CR
  KNOBS[adapter knobs from_env] --> CR[CapResolution.resolve]
  CR -->|min| RD[resolve_deadline]
  RD -->|FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS| FA[fa session clock]
  RD --> DEC[ProgressWatch / ProgressLadder]
  DEC -->|kill_at clamped to cap| KILL[cap_exceeded audit + verdict]
  RD --> AUD[audit: cap + deadline_epoch_ms]
```

</details>

Two defects in the new signal lifecycle:

**1. The `finally` clobbers the process disposition instead of restoring `previous`.**
`loop.remove_signal_handler(sig)` restores CPython's defaults — `SIG_DFL` (or `default_int_handler` for SIGINT) — **not** the captured `previous` (asyncio's `_UnixSelectorEventLoop.remove_signal_handler` has no notion of the prior handler). So after the first supervised trial in a harbor process, the SIGTERM/SIGINT dispositions this PR found at install time are permanently gone: a later process-level SIGTERM takes the default path instead of harbor's graceful handling (the very handler the docstring says is being honored "just a few seconds later"). Fix: in the `finally`, `signal.signal(sig, previous)` when `previous` is a Python-level handler (the machinery already exists — `_rehonor` does exactly this on the flush path). If `previous` is `_sighandler_noop` (harbor had its own `add_signal_handler` registration), the captured value can't restore the loop callback — in that case prefer *not installing* over half-restoring (skip when `signal.getsignal(sig)` is neither `SIG_DFL` nor `default_int_handler`).

**2. Overlapping trials clobber each other (the workflow exposes `--n-concurrent`).**
`bench-harbor.yml` takes an `n-concurrent` input (default 1, owner-raised for kimi). With >1, two FaAgent trials in one loop each call `loop.add_signal_handler(SIGTERM, ...)` — last install wins, and whichever trial finishes first strips the handler the live trial just installed. On a process SIGTERM only one trial's audit flushes; the others leave `running` checkpoints. If concurrent installs are to be supported, make the install refcounted (module-level registry keyed by signal) or document `n-concurrent=1` as a hard requirement for the SIGTERM path.

Minor: the `_rehonor` re-delivery chain is untested — every test passes `previous=None`, so the restore-and-re-kill branch (the production path) has zero coverage. A test with a real `previous` (e.g. a recording function) would pin behavior 1's fix too."

    """Seconds inside a Dart `Duration(...)` constructor call.

    Accepts any argument subset/order (`Duration(seconds: 180)`,

    `Duration(milliseconds: 500)`) — the coupling REG (gh-1430) feeds it

    body = declaration[declaration.index("(") + 1 : declaration.rindex(")")]

        "milliseconds": 0.001,
        "seconds": 1.0,
        "minutes": 60.0,
        "hours": 3600.0,

            total += float(value) * factor

    return total

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1584
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1584
- **Title**: gh-1576 [GOAL] Truthful effective deadline: min(external harness cap, fa knobs) — kill the lying 3600s clock (TB 2.1 external-timeout class)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1576` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 16
- **Additions**: +2198
- **Deletions**: -203
- **Created**: 2026-10-13T10:16:37Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T21:25:26Z

## PR Description

Closes #1576
### What changed

The external harness cap (tb `--global-agent-timeout-sec`, harbor's per-task `[agent] timeout_sec`) is now resolved by the bench adapters and folded into ONE effective deadline — `min(external cap, adapter knobs)` — exported to fa as `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` and recorded truthfully in every audit.

### Key decisions

- `bench/fa_agent_timeout.py` owns resolution: new `CapResolution` (env scan + strict parsing; malformed caps degrade to unknown with a stderr warning) and `resolve_deadline()` as the single source of the effective cap + wrap-up deadline
- Both workflows export the cap: `bench.yml` sets `FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC` = the same number as `--global-agent-timeout-sec` (parity); `bench-harbor.yml` maps `matrix.external_cap` — the MIN of the shard tasks' declared timeouts, resolved pre-launch by `split_tasks.py`; no declared cap ⇒ no export ⇒ knobs rule alone (byte-identical)
- Deciders clamp their kill deadline to the external cap and name the winner (`external_cap`) in the verdict; audits gain `cap` resolution + `deadline_epoch_ms`, and land even on unsupervised external kills (verdict = the harness failure mode — no more bare `AGENT_STATUS_UNSET`)
- Kill-survival hardening: incremental per-sample audit checkpoints survive a SIGKILL; cancellations/SIGTERM flush `outcome=external_kill`; tb's cap regex accepts `s`/`h`/`m` suffixes instead of misparsing `task.toml` text as seconds
- Unknown stays unknown: no invented clocks anywhere (absent/empty/malformed cap ⇒ pre-PR behavior byte-for-byte, pinned by REG tests)

### How to verify

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench -p "test_*.py"   # 402 tests
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa    -p "test_*.py"    # 101 tests
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  WF[workflows: FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC] --> CR
  KNOBS[adapter knobs from_env] --> CR[CapResolution.resolve]
  CR -->|min| RD[resolve_deadline]
  RD -->|FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS| FA[fa session clock]
  RD --> DEC[ProgressWatch / ProgressLadder]
  DEC -->|kill_at clamped to cap| KILL[cap_exceeded audit + verdict]
  RD --> AUD[audit: cap + deadline_epoch_ms]
```

</details>

Two defects in the new signal lifecycle:

**1. The `finally` clobbers the process disposition instead of restoring `previous`.**
`loop.remove_signal_handler(sig)` restores CPython's defaults — `SIG_DFL` (or `default_int_handler` for SIGINT) — **not** the captured `previous` (asyncio's `_UnixSelectorEventLoop.remove_signal_handler` has no notion of the prior handler). So after the first supervised trial in a harbor process, the SIGTERM/SIGINT dispositions this PR found at install time are permanently gone: a later process-level SIGTERM takes the default path instead of harbor's graceful handling (the very handler the docstring says is being honored "just a few seconds later"). That flips the I2 story for anything still in flight: no graceful cancellation → no `external_kill` flushes for other trials → only `running` checkpoints survive (which the aggregation layers then misread — see the honesty-scan comment). Fix: in the `finally`, `signal.signal(sig, previous)` when `previous` is a Python-level handler (the machinery already exists — `_rehonor` does exactly this on the flush path). If `previous` is `_sighandler_noop` (harbor had its own `add_signal_handler` registration), the captured value can't restore the loop callback — in that case prefer *not installing* over half-restoring (skip when `signal.getsignal(sig)` is neither `SIG_DFL` nor `default_int_handler`).

**2. Overlapping trials clobber each other (the workflow exposes `--n-concurrent`).**
`bench-harbor.yml` takes an `n-concurrent` input (default 1, owner-raised for kimi). With >1, two FaAgent trials in one loop each call `loop.add_signal_handler(SIGTERM, ...)` — last install wins, and whichever trial finishes first strips the handler the live trial just installed. On a process SIGTERM only one trial's audit flushes; the others leave `running` checkpoints. If concurrent installs are to be supported, make the install refcounted (module-level registry keyed by signal) or document `n-concurrent=1` as a hard requirement for the SIGTERM path.

Minor: the `_rehonor` re-delivery chain is untested — every test passes `previous=None`, so the restore-and-re-kill branch (the production path) has zero coverage. A test with a real `previous` (e.g. a recording function) would pin behavior 1's fix too."

    def _flush_external_kill(self, signame: str, cause: str, previous=None) -> None:
        """Write the final external_kill audit once, then honor the signal.

        Idempotent against the cancel-path flush (first writer wins).
        With a `previous` disposition (the production signal path), the
        signal is restored and re-delivered to it after the flush —
        the process still dies, the audit just outlives the race.
        """
        if getattr(self, "_external_kill_flushed", False):
            return
        self._external_kill_flushed = True
        environment = getattr(self, "_run_environment", None)

            await self._write_audit(

                cap=getattr(self, "_cap", None),

def _importable(name: str) -> bool:
    # find_spec is not enough: with bench/terminal_bench on sys.path (as
    # unittest discover does), find_spec("terminal_bench") matches the
    # DIRECTORY itself as a namespace package and false-positives.
    try:
        module = importlib.import_module(name)
    except ImportError:
        return False
    # test_progress_watch_adapter installs a stdlib stub package under the
    # same name (so its ITs run where terminal-bench is not installed);
    # a stub is not the real dependency.
    return not getattr(module, "__fa_tb_stub__", False)


TB_AVAILABLE = _importable("terminal_bench.agents.base_agent")
HARBOR_AVAILABLE = _importable("harbor")

KNOB_NAMES = (
    "FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC",
    "FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION",
    "FA_AGENT_IDLE_WINDOW_SEC",
    "FA_AGENT_CEILING_MULTIPLIER",
)

# gh-1576: the external harness cap rides its own env var; every clean-env
# helper must strip it so a host-exported cap cannot leak into a test that
# means to pin the no-cap byte-identity.
EXTERNAL_CAP_NAME = "FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC"


def clean_env(**overrides):
    env = {
        name: value
        for name, value in os.environ.items()
        if name not in KNOB_NAMES + (EXTERNAL_CAP_NAME,)
    }
    env.update(overrides)
    return env


def _dart_duration_seconds(declaration: str) -> float:
    """Seconds inside a Dart `Duration(...)` constructor call.

    Accepts any argument subset/order (`Duration(seconds: 180)`,
    `Duration(minutes: 5)`, `Duration(minutes: 1, seconds: 30)`,
    `Duration(milliseconds: 500)`) — the coupling REG (gh-1430) feeds it
    the `providerStreamIdleTimeout` line from the Dart source, and the
    parse must survive a benign unit change there.
    """
    body = declaration[declaration.index("(") + 1 : declaration.rindex(")")]
    factors = {
        "milliseconds": 0.001,
        "seconds": 1.0,
        "minutes": 60.0,
        "hours": 3600.0,

## PR Description

Closes #1576
### What changed

The external harness cap (tb `--global-agent-timeout-sec`, harbor's per-task `[agent] timeout_sec`) is now resolved by the bench adapters and folded into ONE effective deadline — `min(external cap, adapter knobs)` — exported to fa as `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` and recorded truthfully in every audit.

### Key decisions

- `bench/fa_agent_timeout.py` owns resolution: new `CapResolution` (env scan + strict parsing; malformed caps degrade to unknown with a stderr warning) and `resolve_deadline()` as the single source of the effective cap + wrap-up deadline
- Both workflows export the cap: `bench.yml` sets `FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC` = the same number as `--global-agent-timeout-sec` (parity); `bench-harbor.yml` maps `matrix.external_cap` — the MIN of the shard tasks' declared timeouts, resolved pre-launch by `split_tasks.py`; no declared cap ⇒ no export ⇒ knobs rule alone (byte-identical)
- Deciders clamp their kill deadline to the external cap and name the winner (`external_cap`) in the verdict; audits gain `cap` resolution + `deadline_epoch_ms`, and land even on unsupervised external kills (verdict = the harness failure mode — no more bare `AGENT_STATUS_UNSET`)
- Kill-survival hardening: incremental per-sample audit checkpoints survive a SIGKILL; cancellations/SIGTERM flush `outcome=external_kill`; tb's cap regex accepts `s`/`h`/`m` suffixes instead of misparsing `task.toml` text as seconds
- Unknown stays unknown: no invented clocks anywhere (absent/empty/malformed cap ⇒ pre-PR behavior byte-for-byte, pinned by REG tests)

### How to verify

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench -p "test_*.py"   # 402 tests
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa    -p "test_*.py"    # 101 tests
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  WF[workflows: FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC] --> CR
  KNOBS[adapter knobs from_env] --> CR[CapResolution.resolve]
  CR -->|min| RD[resolve_deadline]
  RD -->|FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS| FA[fa session clock]
  RD --> DEC[ProgressWatch / ProgressLadder]
  DEC -->|kill_at clamped to cap| KILL[cap_exceeded audit + verdict]
  RD --> AUD[audit: cap + deadline_epoch_ms]
```

</details>

    async def _run_external_cap_only(self, instruction: str, environment) -> None:
        """Unsupervised exec under a known external cap (gh-1576).

        The harness owns the kill; the adapter's whole job here is I1+I2:
        fa sees the truthful deadline (via _provider_env) and every
        termination — clean exit, external cancellation, SIGTERM — leaves
        the audit record.
        """
        cap = self._cap
        self._run_environment = environment
        self._external_kill_flushed = False
        try:
            with self._kill_auditors():
                await self.exec_as_agent(
                    environment, command=self._agent_command(instruction),
                    env=self._provider_env,
                )
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            await self._flush_external_kill_audit(
                environment, None, None, cap, cause="cancelled"
            )
            raise
        await self._write_audit(
            environment, None, None, "completed",
            deadline_epoch_ms=self._deadline_epoch_ms,
            cap=cap,
        )

    # ── gh-1576: external-kill audit trail (I2) ──────────────────────────

    @contextmanager
    def _kill_auditors(self):
        """SIGTERM/SIGINT handlers that flush the audit before dying.

        Installed for the duration of a supervised (or external-cap-only)
        run, main thread only, and restored afterwards — harbor's own
        handlers (e.g. jobs.py's SIGTERM→KeyboardInterrupt) are captured
        and re-delivered once the flush lands, so termination semantics

    """Seconds inside a Dart `Duration(...)` constructor call.

    Accepts any argument subset/order (`Duration(seconds: 180)`,

    `Duration(milliseconds: 500)`) — the coupling REG (gh-1430) feeds it

    body = declaration[declaration.index("(") + 1 : declaration.rindex(")")]

        "seconds": 1.0,
        "minutes": 60.0,
        "hours": 3600.0,

        for value in re.findall(rf"\b{name}\s*:\s*([0-9.]+)", body):
